title: Part I. A Guide for Advocates and Planners

h: Alabama's mental health system is not one system. It is a set of systems
— a state agency and its contracted community centers,

and commercial insurers, hospitals and emergency departments, schools, courts and jails, housing coalitions, veterans' services, and nonprofits and faith communities — that together determine whether a person in Alabama can find help, afford it, reach it, and keep it.
No single office sees all of it
This report is an attempt to describe all of it in one place, in plain language
, so that people who want to improve it can see where they stand.
The report has three uses. For
it supplies verified, dated figures and the name of the body responsible for each part of the system
, so that a request to a legislator, a county commission or a foundation can be specific. For
it offers a common structure for deciding where to invest and for recognizing which partner owns the adjacent piece
it gives a baseline against which later editions — and a planned North Alabama regional edition built on the same template — can measure change
The analysis uses eight domains adapted from
the World Health Organization's six "building blocks" of a health system
plus two that this report adds, on equity and on community engagement
— who decides, under what law, with what accountability
— where the money comes from and how it moves
— what services exist, where, for whom
— who delivers care and whether there are enough of them
— how the system knows what it is doing
— who the system reaches and who it misses
— how the public shapes the system
Two lenses run through the report.
